newsitem.title: USA: DHL to buy 7 A300 freighters for US network.
newsitem.headline: DHL to buy 7 A300 freighters for US network.

text.p: DHL Airways, U.S. operating unit of DHL Worldwide Express, said it has signed a memorandum of understanding to buy seven General Electric Co powered Airbus Industrie A300B4 freighters.

Purchase terms were not disclosed. The aircraft are being sold by Airbus, and DHL Airways said in its statement they will be converted into freighters by one of two Airbus partners, either Daimler-Benz Aerospace or British Aerospace Aviation Services.
It is common practice for Airbus, in the process of selling passenger carriers new aircraft, to take older models in trade and remarket them.
DHL is the first operator to acquire converted A300B4 freighters from Airbus.

The twin-engine A300B4 freighters are the first widebody and first Airbus aircraft joining the DHL U.S. fleet. Until now, narrowbody DC-8s have been the mainstay, supported by smaller aircraft including B-727s.

The A300B4s will be based at DHL Airways' main hub at Greater Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky Airport in Covington, Kentucky, with first deliveries scheduled for the second quarter of 1998, continuing through the end of 1999.
DHL did not specify routings but said the A300s would focus on major U.S. cities and possibly Mexico. Each aircraft can lift 95,000 pounds of freight and 20 container load positions, DHL added.
The A300B2/B4 series were the first generation A300 developed by Airbus. The plane has been succeeded in production by the A300-600R.
A total of 243 of the older A300s are flying for the world's airlines, including 19 in freighter configuration, said DHL.
Federal Express operates a fleet of new A300-600 freighters.
